```json
    "languageId": "javascript"
  }
}
```

---

Added a Node-based Faker generator for settlement transactions in your `@portola` project (`portala` folder).

### What I changed
- Created `portala/scripts/generate-settlements.js`:
  - Generates transactions with:
    - `id` (UUID)
    - `clientName`
    - `amountUsd` (number, 2 decimals)
    - `status` (`pending`, `cleared`, `failed`)
    - `timestamp` (ISO string)
  - Supports optional count arg (default `10`), e.g. `... 25`.
- Updated `portala/package.json`:
  - Added script: `generate:settlements`
  - Added dependency: `@faker-js/faker`

### Run it
From `portala`:
- `npm install`
- `npm run generate:settlements`
- Optional count: `npm run generate:settlements -- 20`

### Note
I couldn’t execute runtime verification in this environment due a shell spawn issue (`powershell.exe ENOENT`), but the files are in place and lint checks reported no issues for the edited files.

```json
    "codeBlockIdx": 0,
    "content": "const { faker } = require(\"@faker-js/faker\");\r\n\r\nconst STATUSES = [\"pending\", \"cleared\", \"failed\"];\r\nconst DEFAULT_COUNT = 10;\r\nconst SMALL_AMOUNT_MAX = 999.99;\r\nconst LARGE_AMOUNT_MIN = 50000.01;\r\n\r\nfunction randomStatus() {\r\n  return faker.helpers.arrayElement(STATUSES);\r\n}\r\n\r\nfunction randomAmount(min, max) {\r\n  return Number(faker.finance.amount({ min, max, dec: 2 }));\r\n}\r\n\r\nfunction generateSettlementTransaction(amountRange = { min: 100, max: 10000 }) {\r\n  return {\r\n    id: faker.string.uuid(),\r\n    clientName: faker.person.fullName(),\r\n    amountUsd: randomAmount(amountRange.min, amountRange.max),\r\n    status: randomStatus(),\r\n    timestamp: faker.date.recent({ days: 30 }).toISOString(),\r\n  };\r\n}\r\n\r\nfunction generateSettlementTransactions(count = DEFAULT_COUNT) {\r\n  return Array.from({ length: count }, generateSettlementTransaction);\r\n}\r\n\r\nfunction generateMixedAmountSettlementTransactions(count = 50) {\r\n  const smallCount = Math.max(1, Math.floor(count / 2));\r\n  const largeCount = Math.max(1, count - smallCount);\r\n  const smallTransactions = Array.from({ length: smallCount }, () =&gt;\r\n    generateSettlementTransaction({ min: 10, max: SMALL_AMOUNT_MAX })\r\n  );\r\n  const largeTransactions = Array.from({ length: largeCount }, () =&gt;\r\n    generateSettlementTransaction({ min: LARGE_AMOUNT_MIN, max: 250000 })\r\n  );\r\n\r\n  return faker.helpers.shuffle([...smallTransactions, ...largeTransactions]);\r\n}\r\n\r\nfunction parseCountArg(rawArg) {\r\n  const parsed = Number(rawArg);\r\n\r\n  if (!Number.isInteger(parsed) || parsed &lt;= 0) {\r\n    return DEFAULT_COUNT;\r\n  }\r\n\r\n  return parsed;\r\n}\r\n\r\nif (require.main === module) {\r\n  const countArg = process.argv[2];\r\n  const modeArg = process.argv[3];\r\n  const count = countArg ? parseCountArg(countArg) : DEFAULT_COUNT;\r\n  const transactions =\r\n    modeArg === \"mixed\"\r\n      ? generateMixedAmountSettlementTransactions(count)\r\n      : generateSettlementTransactions(count);\r\n\r\n  console.log(JSON.stringify(transactions, null, 2));\r\n}\r\n\r\nmodule.exports = {\r\n  generateSettlementTransaction,\r\n  generateSettlementTransactions,\r\n  generateMixedAmountSettlementTransactions,\r\n  SMALL_AMOUNT_MAX,\r\n  LARGE_AMOUNT_MIN,\r\n};\r\n",
    "languageId": "javascript"
  }
}
```

```json
  "contentsAfterEdit": "const { faker } = require(\"@faker-js/faker\");\r\n\r\nconst STATUSES = [\"pending\", \"cleared\", \"failed\"];\r\nconst DEFAULT_COUNT = 10;\r\nconst SMALL_AMOUNT_MAX = 999.99;\r\nconst LARGE_AMOUNT_MIN = 50000.01;\r\n\r\nfunction randomStatus() {\r\n  return faker.helpers.arrayElement(STATUSES);\r\n}\r\n\r\nfunction randomAmount(min, max) {\r\n  return Number(faker.finance.amount({ min, max, dec: 2 }));\r\n}\r\n\r\nfunction generateSettlementTransaction(amountRange = { min: 100, max: 10000 }) {\r\n  return {\r\n    id: faker.string.uuid(),\r\n    clientName: faker.person.fullName(),\r\n    amountUsd: randomAmount(amountRange.min, amountRange.max),\r\n    status: randomStatus(),\r\n    timestamp: faker.date.recent({ days: 30 }).toISOString(),\r\n  };\r\n}\r\n\r\nfunction generateSettlementTransactions(count = DEFAULT_COUNT) {\r\n  return Array.from({ length: count }, generateSettlementTransaction);\r\n}\r\n\r\nfunction generateMixedAmountSettlementTransactions(count = 50) {\r\n  const smallCount = Math.max(1, Math.floor(count / 2));\r\n  const largeCount = Math.max(1, count - smallCount);\r\n  const smallTransactions = Array.from({ length: smallCount }, () =&gt;\r\n    generateSettlementTransaction({ min: 10, max: SMALL_AMOUNT_MAX })\r\n  );\r\n  const largeTransactions = Array.from({ length: largeCount }, () =&gt;\r\n    generateSettlementTransaction({ min: LARGE_AMOUNT_MIN, max: 250000 })\r\n  );\r\n\r\n  return faker.helpers.shuffle([...smallTransactions, ...largeTransactions]);\r\n}\r\n\r\nfunction parseCountArg(rawArg) {\r\n  const parsed = Number(rawArg);\r\n\r\n  if (!Number.isInteger(parsed) || parsed &lt;= 0) {\r\n    return DEFAULT_COUNT;\r\n  }\r\n\r\n  return parsed;\r\n}\r\n\r\nif (require.main === module) {\r\n  const countArg = process.argv[2];\r\n  const modeArg = process.argv[3];\r\n  const count = countArg ? parseCountArg(countArg) : DEFAULT_COUNT;\r\n  const transactions =\r\n    modeArg === \"mixed\"\r\n      ? generateMixedAmountSettlementTransactions(count)\r\n      : generateSettlementTransactions(count);\r\n\r\n  console.log(JSON.stringify(transactions, null, 2));\r\n}\r\n\r\nmodule.exports = {\r\n  generateSettlementTransaction,\r\n  generateSettlementTransactions,\r\n  generateMixedAmountSettlementTransactions,\r\n  SMALL_AMOUNT_MAX,\r\n  LARGE_AMOUNT_MIN,\r\n};\r\n"
}
```

Implemented a Playwright test suite in `@portola` (`portala`) for the 50-transaction mixed-amount scenario.

### What I changed
- Refactored `portala/scripts/generate-settlements.js` to export reusable functions.
- Added a new generator: `generateMixedAmountSettlementTransactions(count)` that guarantees a mix of:
  - small amounts `< 1,000`
  - large amounts `> 50,000`
- Kept CLI behavior and added a `mixed` mode:
  - `node scripts/generate-settlements.js 50 mixed`
- Added Playwright config: `portala/playwright.config.js`
- Added test file: `portala/tests/settlement-generator.spec.js`
  - Verifies:
    - exactly 50 transactions
    - required fields exist and are valid
    - statuses are `pending|cleared|failed`
    - at least one small and one large transaction
- Updated `portala/package.json` scripts:
  - `generate:settlements`
  - `generate:settlements:mixed`
  - `test:settlements`
- Added ignore entries for Playwright outputs in `portala/.gitignore`.

### Run it
From `portala`:
- `npm install`
- `npm run test:settlements`
- Optional data run: `npm run generate:settlements:mixed`

I interpreted your `50,0000` as `50,000+`. If you meant `500,000+`, I can switch the threshold in one quick edit.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>
**Redesigning pending transactions flow**</details></think>

---

I found one important side effect: with the 2-second simulator always on, tests and “all clear” behavior become nondeterministic. I’m adding a provider flag to disable simulation in tests, then wiring an explicit `allowPendingTransactions` action that the UI button triggers.

---

Updated. New incoming transactions now remain `pending` until the user explicitly approves them.

### What changed
- `portala/context/transactions-context.tsx`
  - Removed automatic timed resolution.
  - Added `allowPendingTransactions()` to resolve all currently pending rows on demand.
  - Kept the 2-second simulation feed.
  - Added optional `simulateIncoming` prop on provider (defaults to `true`) so tests can run deterministically.

- `portala/app/page.tsx`
  - Wired `allowPendingTransactions` into UI:
    - Banner now includes **Allow pending** action.
    - Footer shows **Allow pending transactions** button whenever pending items exist.
  - Existing scroll-stability behavior remains in place.

- Tests updated for the new behavior:
  - `portala/tests/transactions.context.test.tsx`
  - `portala/tests/transactions.page.test.tsx`
  - Both now assert “pending until approval,” and use `simulateIncoming={false}` where deterministic behavior is needed.

### Note
There is one remaining lint/module error until dependencies are installed:
- `framer-motion` module not found in `portala/app/page.tsx`

Run this in `portala`:
- `npm install`

If you want, I can also change the wording to be stricter (e.g., “Approve new transactions” everywhere) and make the button sticky near the table header.

Implemented: live data now uses a **staged queue** and does **not** change the grid until the user allows it.

### What changed

- `portala/context/transactions-context.tsx`
  - Added internal `queuedIncomingTransactions` buffer.
  - Live simulation (`2s`) now appends to queue only, not to visible `transactions`.
  - `allowPendingTransactions()` now flushes queued items into the top of `transactions` as `pending`.
  - Exposed `queuedIncomingCount` in context.

- `portala/app/page.tsx`
  - Banner now reflects queued items (`queuedIncomingCount`) rather than table-diff detection.
  - Banner CTA changed to **Allow queued**.
  - Footer status now distinguishes:
    - queued live updates waiting for approval
    - existing visible pending rows needing manual clear
  - Grid stays visually stable until approval.

- Tests updated for new behavior:
  - `portala/tests/transactions.context.test.tsx`
    - Verifies queue increments after 2s and grid count is unchanged until allow.
  - `portala/tests/transactions.page.test.tsx`
    - Verifies queued banner appears and total transaction count only increases after allow.

- `framer-motion` not resolved in `portala/app/page.tsx`

---

I’m now patching `lib/transactions` to make fallback seed mixed-status, and switching context to use the dedicated live generator (so queued arrivals stay pending with the new 10% high-value rule). Then I’ll relax brittle test assumptions around “all pending.”

---

Implemented both changes.

- Live queued transactions now have a **10% chance** to be high value (`>= $50,000`), otherwise they stay below `$50,000`.
- Default seeded transactions now start with a **mixed status distribution** (`pending`, `cleared`, `failed`) instead of all pending.

### Updated files
- `portala/lib/transactions.ts`
  - `createFallbackTransactions()` now generates mixed initial statuses.
  - `createLiveIncomingTransaction()` now applies the 10% high-value rule.
- `portala/context/transactions-context.tsx`
  - Live queue generation now enforces:
    - pending status for newly queued items
    - 10% high-value amount logic
- `portala/tests/transactions.context.test.tsx`
  - Relaxed assumptions from “all initial rows pending” to dynamic pending baseline.
- `portala/tests/transactions.page.test.tsx`
  - Pending-row assertion now adapts to mixed seeded statuses.

### Lint status
- Only one existing issue remains (unrelated to this change set):
  - `portala/tests/transactions.page.test.tsx` cannot resolve `@tanstack/react-query` types/module in current environment.

```json
    "content": "## Portola Overview\r\n\r\n&#96;Portola&#96; contains a Next.js app (&#96;portala&#96;) that simulates settlement activity with queued live updates and manual approval workflows.\r\n\r\n### Project Structure\r\n\r\n- &#96;portala/app/&#96; - UI routes, main dashboard page, app layout/providers\r\n- &#96;portala/context/&#96; - React Context state container for transaction lifecycle\r\n- &#96;portala/lib/&#96; - transaction/domain logic and mock API helpers\r\n- &#96;portala/scripts/&#96; - Node + Faker data generators (including mixed amount profiles)\r\n- &#96;portala/tests/&#96; - Vitest + RTL tests and Playwright checks\r\n- &#96;.specstory/&#96; - AI session history and project-level interaction artifacts\r\n\r\n### Approach (from &#96;.specstory&#96; sessions)\r\n\r\n- Start with script-first data generation using Faker, then plug into UI state.\r\n- Centralize transaction state in React Context for shared, testable behavior.\r\n- Use staged live-ingest: queue incoming rows, show banner, apply only on user approval.\r\n- Keep UX safe under live updates (scroll anchoring + explicit allow actions).\r\n- Back behavior with focused tests for logic, context state, page UX, and generator output.\r\n\r\n### Startup\r\n\r\n1. &#96;cd portala&#96;\r\n2. &#96;npm install&#96;\r\n3. &#96;npm run dev&#96;\r\n4. Open &#96;http://localhost:3000&#96;\r\n\r\nOptional commands:\r\n- &#96;npm run test&#96; (Vitest suite)\r\n- &#96;npm run test:settlements&#96; (Playwright settlement generator check)\r\n- &#96;npm run generate:settlements:mixed&#96; (prints 50 mixed mock transactions)",
```
